children: An energy storage company will supply Alphabet-owned Google with data-center batteries for a project in West Virginia, under a collaboration announced Wednesday aimed at improving grid stability in the Midwestern and Mid-Atlantic regions.

Shares of Eos Energy Enterprises, a manufacturer of zinc-based energy storage systems, rose 19% to $3.63 on Wednesday. The gains came after the company announced it was working with MN8 Energy, one of the nation's largest independent solar energy producers, to power Google's data centers, including the West Virginia facility.

The move marks that state's first commercial-scale deployment of long-duration storage, and Google's first use of Eos' zinc-based technology. The initiative is set to roll out from 2028 to 2030. MN8 Energy will spend $350 million on the new facility and then operate it, according to a press release.

The project is a major win for Eos, which has struggled to achieve profitability since going public in 2020. Although revenue surged 351% to $68.8 million in the fiscal second quarter, the company still posted a loss of $1.20 a share.
Eos did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Barron's regarding projected partnership revenue.
Truist Securities analyst Christopher Souther noted that while the announcement Wednesday is encouraging, investors continue to wait for sustained financial improvement.

Eos is supplying Google with a system that can hold up to 10 hours of energy, stretching solar power far past what standard batteries can cover to provide reliable electricity around the clock. The project will test whether Eos' zinc-based technology can support heavy-duty power grids.

"The grid needs more from every megawatt of new generation," Chief Commercial Officer Nathan Kroeker said in a statement. "Our work with Google is focused on deploying American-made long-duration storage where it solves real grid reliability challenges."

The power will feed into PJM Interconnection, the regional grid serving West Virginia and 12 other Mid-Atlantic and Midwestern states, with the goal of supplying regional factories and tech facilities with reliable electricity.

In a bid to scale production and cut costs, Eos has been consolidating manufacturing into an automated Pennsylvania factory-a move Souther expects to boost operational efficiency. The analyst rates Eos at Buy with a $7 price target.
